audits.text:
## 34e41cf35fde

**Reproduced shortcut and validator defect; target left unchanged.** Audited
generator SHA-256
`ba87c1ba595b7fdcb1ea6473c9f3db36a2837f6337480081ce605a5e8d94ea20`;
the generator declares no `RULE_HASH`. Canonical program SHA-256 is
`88e163b0ffa81ff348e8792689233c8f4d2d83c88a02c8f01ada58d941f93761`.
The assignment hash matched the inspected bytes.

The ordinary constructor always places the selected red object's bottom on row
`h-1` or `h-2`. Consequently, the rival “recolor the unique red component that
touches either of the final two rows; otherwise do nothing” matched:

- 3/3 canonical train/test pairs;
- 1,000/1,000 easy samples (970 unique);
- 1,000/1,000 default samples (999 unique);
- 1,000/1,000 hard samples (1,000 unique).

All 3,000 generated inputs had a unique lowest object, exactly one component
reaching the final two rows, and zero validator failures. Seeds were the audit
assignment seed suffixed with `:34:<band>`, indexes 0–999. Full denominators and
hashes are in `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/probe.json`.

The counterexample in `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/input.json` obeys the documented
task invariants—background 0, all objects red, and one unique lowest object—and
`self_check` returns no errors. It deliberately places all objects above the
last two rows. Thus it belongs to the documented task domain and passes the
validator, but it does **not** belong to the ordinary generated support; that
support restriction is the shortcut. The real Racket authority recolors the
lowest object at rows 5–6, while the bottom-two rival leaves the grid unchanged:

- metadata: `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/counterexample.json`;
- supported authority output: `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/racket.json`;
- rival output: `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/rival_output.json`.

Racket command, from packet root:
`python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 34e41cf35fde --input ../checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/input.json --out ../checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/racket.json`
(exit 0; log `checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/apply-command.log`).

The validator also conflates red cells with red objects. A single connected
2-cell red object is accepted even though the docstring says at least two
distinct objects are required. Reproducer:
`checks/audit/34e41cf35fde/validator_counterexample.json`.

Control metadata is also inconsistent: advertised globally valid `grid_h=7`,
`grid_h=14`, `grid_w=7`, and `grid_w=16` are rejected in the default band because
the implementation passes narrower difficulty-local ranges to `draw_int`, while
an unknown override is accepted. These are reproduced in the same probe report.
